1.w: [“] Behold, all [this] my eye has seen; my ear has heard and understood it.

2.w: According to your⁺ knowledge, I also know; I am not falling below you⁺.

3.w: But I wish to speak to Shaddai, and to reason with God I desire.

4.w: But you⁺, are plasterers of a lie, worthless physicians all of you⁺.

5.w: Who will give [that] you will surely remain silent, and it will be for wisdom for you⁺.

6.w: Hear now my reasoning, and be attentive to the quarreling of my lips.

7.w: Will you⁺ speak injustice for God, and will you⁺ speak deceit for Him?

8.w: Will you⁺ lift His face, or will you⁺ contend for God?

9.w: Will [it be] good when He searches you⁺ out? Or as one mocks a man, can you⁺ mock Him?

10.w: He will surely rebuke you⁺, if in secrecy you⁺ were lifting faces.

11.w: Will not His excellence terrify you⁺ and the dread of Him fall upon you⁺?

12.w: Your⁺ remembrances [are] proverbs of ashes; your⁺ defenses [are] defenses of clay.

13.w: Keep silent from me, and I will speak, and let come upon me what may.

14.w: For what do I take up my flesh in my teeth, and my soul do I set in my palm?

15.w: Behold, He may slay me; unto Him I will hope. Indeed, my ways to His face I will defend.

16.w: Even this [may be] unto me salvation, for the godless one shall not come [in] before His face.

17.w: Listen [with] hearing [to] my speech, and may my declaration [be] in your⁺ ears.

18.w: Behold, now, I have arranged my defense. I know that I am righteous.

19.w: Who [is] he [who] will contend with me? For then I would be silent and die.

20.w: Only two [things] may You not do with me; then from Your face I will not hide myself.

21.w: Withdraw your hand from me, and do not let Your terror terrify me.

22.w: And call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and You reply.

23.w: How many [are] the iniquities and sins for me? Make me know my transgression and my sin.

24.w: Why do You hide Your face and consider me as an enemy unto You?

25.w: Would You make tremble a leaf driven away, and would You pursue dry stubble?

26.w: For You write against me bitter [things], and you make me inherit the iniquities of my youth.

27.w: And You put my feet in the stock, and You watch all my paths; upon the soles of my feet You engrave.

28.w: And he, like a rotten thing, is worn out, like a garment a moth has eaten.
